Flag events to keep when thinning tracks by distance travelled

Source: R/event_flag_thin_distance.R
event_flag_thin_distance.Rd

This function selects, within each track, events spaced by the distance travelled along the track. It is a wrapper around move2utils::mt_thin_distance(), which requires the suggested package move2utils (install it with remotes::install_github("move2universe/move2utils")).

Usage

event_flag_thin_distance(
  x,
  distance,
  tolerance = NULL,
  method = c("step", "interval"),
  criterion = c("closest", "first")
)

Arguments

x

A move2 object.

distance

The target distance travelled between consecutive kept events, as a units object (e.g. as_units(500, "m")).

tolerance

Only used with method = "interval": the accepted deviation from distance, as a units object with length units. Defaults to distance / 10.

method

The thinning method, either "step" (the default) or "interval" (see Details).

criterion

Only used with method = "interval": how to choose among subsets with the same number of events. "closest" (the default) keeps the subset whose distances deviate least from distance in total, "first" keeps the subset that starts earliest.

Value

A logical vector with one value per event of x, TRUE for the events to keep.

Details

Two methods are available:

  • method = "step" (the default) keeps the first event of each track, and then the first event at which the distance travelled since the last kept event reaches distance. Consecutive kept events are therefore at least distance apart along the track (and can be further apart, as no new locations are interpolated).

  • method = "interval" keeps the largest subset of events such that the distance travelled between consecutive kept events is distance (plus or minus tolerance); it is the equivalent of event_flag_thin_time() for distances. Tracks are split at any step longer than distance + tolerance, and the first event is not necessarily kept.

Distances are great-circle distances for longitude/latitude coordinates, and planar distances for projected coordinates. Events without a location are ignored when measuring distances, and are never kept. x must be ordered by time within each track (see tt_order_time()). To remove the events that are not kept, use tt_thin_distance().

Examples

# keep events at least 200 km apart along each track
event_flag_thin_distance(example_tt, distance = as_units(200, "km"))
#>  [1]  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE FALSE  TRUE  TRUE FALSE  TRUE  TRUE FALSE  TRUE  TRUE
#> [13] FALSE FALSE  TRUE
